thread.title: Tuning Out SiriusXM's (SIRI) Takeover Bid For Pandora (P) Is a Mistake

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Tuning Out SiriusXM's (SIRI) Takeover Bid For Pandora (P) Is a Mistake
text:
Shutterstock photo Shares of music streaming giant Pandora Media ( P ) and satellite radio provider Sirius XM ( SIRI ) had initially dipped after the latter announced that it would acquire the former in an all-stock transaction.
The deal, which valued Pandora $10.14 per share, will cost Sirius $3.5 billion. Sirius shares got punished on the news, closing down 10.3%. Pandora, meanwhile, which at one point traded as high as 10% Monday, finished down 1.1%. An argument can be made that Pandora just traded with the market. After all, the Dow ended down 181 points, amid heated trade tensions. Sirius, on the other hand, had been on a steady decline throughout the day, falling even in the pre-market session.
Paying $3.5 billion for Pandora — an asset some believe is no more than an internet DJ — is looked upon as throwing good money after bad . The Oakland, Calif.-based company continues to struggle with profitability, pressured not only by high content acquisition costs, but also from increased competition with internet music powers such as Apple ( AAPL ) and Spotify ( SPOT ). And to say nothing about competing music services from Google’s ( GOOG , GOOGL ) YouTube and Amazon ( AMZN ).
So, what does Sirius, which already owned a 15% stake in Pandora which it purchased a year ago, stand to gain by buying Pandora outright?
Before we answer this question, let’s recall that this deal was a year in the making. The New York Post last year suggesting that Sirius, backed by Liberty Media, had held discussions with Pandora about a possible merger. And Pandora at the time had made it known that it was aggressively seeking to sell. A year ago, this deal would have cost Sirius around $12 to $14 per share. At the mid point, Sirius saves 22% in premiums or $2.30 per share. So maybe Sirius sees value.
Sirius, which is a subscription service, compared to Pandora’s freemium model, also understands that this tie-up would help both companies leverage each other’s strengths. Unlike Pandora, Sirius has a proven model that generates tons of free cash flow and can put Pandora on firmer financial footing. At the same time, acquiring Pandora 80 million active listeners gives Sirius more leverage with market leaders Apple and Spotify.
What’s more, being the nation’s lone satellite radio provider give Sirius the flexibility it needs to experiment with Pandora’s ad-based model that, despite its lack of free cash flow, appeals to listeners who don't want to pay for radio. This means the cross-promotional opportunities between the two platforms could be an enormous win for Sirius. Not to mention, any success generated by the deal would immediately catapult Sirius into an acquisition target of its own.
